reasoning: In March 2016, Google DeepMind's AlphaGo competed against Lee Sedol, a 9-dan professional who held 18 international titles and was widely considered the top Go player of the era. AlphaGo won the match 4 games to 1, with Lee Sedol winning only the fourth game. Prior to AlphaGo's success (first demonstrated against European champion Fan Hui in late 2015 and then Lee Sedol in 2016), artificial intelligence experts and Go players widely believed that a computer defeating a top human professional was at least a decade away, making this achievement roughly ten years ahead of most expert projections.
